How does SCRIPE enforce Sovereign Account Security, Passkeys, and Perimeter Isolation?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE protects administrative access through W3C WebAuthn Level 3 Passkeys, Enterprise SSO Identity Federation, and Subnet CIDR Perimeter Enforcement.1

  1. Hardware passkeys eliminate credential theft via unpadded Base64Url normalization (RFC 4648 §5) and FIDO2 AAGUID model resolution.2
  2. PasskeyController and Fido2WebAuthnService verify CBOR attestation and COSE public keys with zero external cloud dependencies.3
  3. Enterprise SSO (/api/v1/auth/admin/external-logins) binds OIDC and SAML 2.0 identities with audit logging and single-click unlinking.4
  4. Trusted CIDR allowlists restrict administrative operations to designated workstation subnets with 15-minute biometric sudo step-up.5

How does the W3C WebAuthn Level 3 ceremony register and authenticate hardware passkeys?

Diagram structure
  • Administrator user
  • WebAuthn Browser API client
  • PasskeyController API gateway
  • Fido2WebAuthnService fido2
  • Passkey & Challenge DB storage
  • user → client · Initiate Passkey Registration
  • client → gateway · POST /registration/begin (JWT)
  • gateway → fido2 · BeginRegistrationAsync(adminId, rpId)
  • fido2 → storage · Store 32-Byte Challenge (5m TTL)
  • storage → fido2 · Challenge Stored
  • fido2 → gateway · CreationOptions (ES256, RS256, EdDSA)
  • gateway → client · 200 OK Creation Options
  • client → user · Prompt Sensor Touch / Enclave KeyGen
  • user → client · Touch ID / Windows Hello / Token Touch
  • client → gateway · POST /registration/complete (Attestation + ClientData)
  • gateway → fido2 · CompleteRegistrationAsync(attestation, clientData)
  • fido2 → storage · Persist AdminPasskey (COSE Key, SignCount, AAGUID)
  • storage → gateway · AdminPasskey Saved
  • gateway → client · 201 Created Passkey Registered
  • user → client · Initiate Passwordless Login
  • client → gateway · POST /authentication/begin (RP ID)
  • gateway → fido2 · BeginAuthenticationAsync()
  • fido2 → gateway · PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions
  • gateway → client · 200 OK Assertion Options
  • client → user · Prompt Biometric or Hardware Assertion
  • user → client · User Verified / Enclave Signs Challenge
  • client → gateway · POST /authentication/verify (Assertion + Signature)
  • gateway → fido2 · VerifyAssertionAsync(challenge, signature, signCount)
  • fido2 → gateway · Assertion Verified (Clone Counter Valid)
  • gateway → client · 200 OK Access Granted (JWT + Refresh Cookie)
  1. Initiate Registration ↗

    Client requests creation options and receives a cryptographically secure 32-byte challenge.

  2. Biometric Sensor Touch ↗

    Device hardware generates a fresh asymmetric keypair inside the secure enclave.

  3. Verify Attestation ↗

    Backend validates CBOR attestation, extracts the COSE public key, and stores the initial sign counter.

  4. Request Assertion Challenge ↗

    Passwordless login begins with a fresh server challenge and allowed credential descriptors.

  5. Validate Assertion Signature ↗

    Server verifies the assertion signature against the stored public key and confirms signCount increased.

How does WebAuthnChallengeHelper normalize RFC 4648 §5 challenges and resolve hardware AAGUIDs?

Standard Specification
W3C WebAuthn Level 3 (Recommendation) & FIDO2 CTAP 2.1
Challenge Encoding
RFC 4648 §5 unpadded Base64Url (-, _, stripped =)
Supported Cryptography
COSE -7 (ES256 ECDSA P-256), -257 (RS256 RSA 2048), -8 (EdDSA)
Authenticator Modes
Platform (Touch ID, Windows Hello) and Cross-Platform (YubiKey, Titan)
Cloning Prevention
Monotonically increasing signature counter (signCount) validation

Web browsers send challenges with variable padding. WebAuthnChallengeHelper normalizes challenges into three canonical representations to guarantee lookup success across memory cache and SQL stores.2

How does Enterprise SSO Identity Federation bind OIDC and SAML 2.0 accounts?

Diagram structure
  • Enterprise IdP (OIDC/SAML2) idp
  • /api/v1/auth/admin/external-logins/link callback
  • AstraFlow Mediator mediator
  • LinkAdminExternalAccountHandler handler
  • ExternalLogin Record entity
  • AuditService Security Log audit
  • NotificationService Alert notify
  • callback → mediator · Send LinkAdminExternalAccountCommand
  • handler → audit · Record AuditEventTypes.ExternalLoginLinked
  • handler → entity · Bind ExternalLogin (ProviderKey, Email)
  • handler → notify · Dispatch Security Notification
  • idp → callback · OIDC Callback (Claims + Subject ID)
  • mediator → handler · Dispatch Command

Enterprise SSO supports Dual-Mode identity binding. Administrators authenticate using corporate single sign-on while preserving hardware passkeys as fallback credentials.4

How does the Interactive CIDR Perimeter Allowlist and Step-Up WebAuthn protect admin endpoints?

Diagram structure
  • Admin Workstation admin
  • AccountSecurityView UI ui
  • CIDR Filter Middleware mw
  • Biometric Sudo Guard sudo
  • Redis Session Cache redis
  • admin → mw · Ingress HTTP Request
  • mw → redis · Check Client IP Against Trusted Subnets
  • redis → mw · Subnet Authorized
  • mw → admin · 200 OK Permitted to Proceed
  • admin → ui · Request Sensitive Policy Change
  • ui → sudo · Verify Sudo Mode Token
  • sudo → admin · Prompt WebAuthn Step-Up Assertion
  • admin → sudo · Hardware Passkey Confirmed
  • sudo → ui · Issue 15-Minute Sudo Session Token
  • admin → ui · Activate Emergency Account Lockdown
  • ui → redis · Blacklist All Active JWTs in IAccountRevocationCache
  • redis → ui · All Sessions Terminated & Account Locked
  • ui → admin · Account Frozen (Recovery Key Required)

Fail-Closed Perimeter & Nuclear Lockdown Invariant

The CIDR perimeter evaluates client IP addresses before any handler execution. Activating Nuclear Account Lockdown immediately blacklists all active JWTs in Redis and terminates all administrative sessions across all devices.5
